Positive real numbers \( x, y, \) and \( z \) satisfy the following equations:

\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let

\[
s=x+y+z,\qquad p=xy+yz+zx.
\]

Then

\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=sp-xyz=sp-3=40,
\]

so

\[
sp=43.
\]

The numbers \(x,y,z\) are the roots of

\[
f(t)=t^3-st^2+pt-3.
\]

Its discriminant is

\[
((x-y)(y-z)(z-x))^2=16.
\]

Using the standard discriminant formula for a monic cubic,

\[
\Delta=s^2p^2-4p^3-4s^3\cdot 3-27\cdot 3^2+18s p\cdot 3,
\]

and substituting \(p=43/s\), we get

\[
16=3928-12s^3-\frac{4\cdot 43^3}{s^3}.
\]

Let \(u=s^3\). Then

\[
3u^2-978u+79507=0,
\]

so

\[
u=\frac{489\pm 10\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

The smaller sum \(s=\sqrt[3]{u}\) gives the smaller minimum root, so we take

\[
u=\frac{489-10\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Now solve the cubic

\[
t^3-st^2+\frac{43}{s}t-3=0
\]

by Cardano. Put \(t=s/3+m\). Then

\[
m^3+pm+q=0,
\]

where

\[
p=\frac{129-u}{3s},\qquad q=\frac{306-2u}{27}.
\]

Using the quadratic relation for \(u\),

\[
\left(\frac q2\right)^2+\left(\frac p3\right)^3=-\frac4{27}.
\]

Thus a Cardano auxiliary value is

\[
\zeta=-\frac q2+\sqrt{-\frac4{27}}
=\frac{u-153}{27}+\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{-3}.
\]

For \(u=\dfrac{489-10\sqrt6}{3}\),

\[
\zeta=\frac{10(3-\sqrt6)}{81}+\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{-3}.
\]

Let the cube roots below be the conjugate principal cube roots (the first one has positive real and positive imaginary parts). Then the smallest root is

\[
\boxed{
\sqrt[3]{\frac{489-10\sqrt6}{81}}
+\left(-\frac12+\frac12\sqrt{-3}\right)
\sqrt[3]{\frac{10(3-\sqrt6)}{81}+\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{-3}}
+\left(-\frac12-\frac12\sqrt{-3}\right)
\sqrt[3]{\frac{10(3-\sqrt6)}{81}-\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{-3}}
}
\]
